- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if price is trending down.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) are common; apply downward correction of 5-10% in next 5-7 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate with mean-reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >15% above model, check if sentiment was bullish early; if so, model likely overreacted; apply downward bias of 5-8%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.33), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 7-day moving average as anchor for correction.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 3-5% for next 10 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome and sentiment is positive, consider “sentiment fatigue” — reduce forecast by 5-10% for next 5 days.
